records.name: Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF)
records.opportunity_type: Government-backed loan with interest subvention and, for qualifying MSME projects, credit guarantee
objective: Increase milk and meat processing capacity and product diversification, providing greater access for unorganized rural milk and meat producers to organized markets.
Provide increased price realization for producers.
Make quality milk and meat products available to domestic consumers.
Support protein-enriched quality food requirements and help prevent malnutrition.
Promote exports and increase export contribution in the milk and meat sector.
Make quality concentrated animal feed available to cattle, buffalo, sheep, goat, pig and poultry at affordable prices.
records.legal_basis: Implementation Guidelines for Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF)

authority.name: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India

dairy_processing: Establishment of new dairy processing units.
Strengthening of existing dairy processing units with quality and hygienic milk processing facilities, packaging facilities or other activities related to dairy processing.
value_added_dairy_product_manufacturing: Ultra High Temperature (UHT) milk processing units with tetra packaging facilities.
Other milk products and value-addition manufacturing units.
meat_processing_and_value_addition: Establishment of new meat processing units and strengthening of existing meat processing facilities for sheep, goat, poultry, pig and buffalo in rural, semi-urban and urban areas.
Large-scale integrated meat processing facilities, plants or units.
New or strengthened value-addition facilities for sausage, nuggets, ham, salami, bacon or other meat products, either integral to meat processing units or as standalone meat value-addition units.
animal_feed: Mini, medium and large animal feed plants.
Animal feed testing laboratories attached to medium-to-large feed plants or established in existing feed plants to ensure quality feed.

project_conditions: Meat processing plant project cost must compulsorily include an Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP), meat microbiological testing laboratory, residue testing laboratory, cold storage for holding offals, skin/hide processing areas and preservation and refrigeration facilities for holding chilled products and value-added products for a minimum of 24 hours.
eligibility.loan_condition: Loan eligibility is based on submission of viable projects by eligible beneficiaries to a Scheduled Bank.

records.benefit_summary: Eligible projects may receive a loan of up to 90% of estimated or actual project cost from a Scheduled Bank, with beneficiary contribution requirements varying by enterprise category. All Eligible Entities may receive 3% interest subvention, subject to the stated conditions. Viable projects covered under MSME-defined ceilings may also receive credit guarantee coverage of up to 25% of the credit facility available to the borrower.

benefits.amount_or_rate: Up to 90% of the estimated or actual project cost
benefits.conditions: Loan is provided by a Scheduled Bank based on submission of a viable project by an eligible beneficiary.

benefits.amount_or_rate: 10% for Micro and Small units as per MSME-defined ceiling; up to 15% for Medium Enterprises as per MSME-defined ceiling; up to 25% for other categories of enterprises
benefits.conditions: Contribution levels are stated in section 7.1.

Available for all Eligible Entities, subject to the guidelines. It is not allowed for loans sanctioned for procurement of land, working capital, old machinery or vehicles for personal use, and is unavailable if the Eligible Entity defaults on loan repayment in any given year.

benefits.amount_or_rate: Up to 25% of the credit facility available to the borrower
benefits.conditions: Available only for viable projects covered under MSME-defined ceilings. The guidelines state that the guarantee will not be provided to beneficiaries outside MSME norms, although those Eligible Entities remain eligible for interest subvention. The Credit Guarantee Fund is stated as Rs. 750 cr. and will be managed by NABARD.

benefits.amount_or_rate: Maximum repayment period stated as 8 years inclusive of a 2-year moratorium on principal
benefits.conditions: The guidelines also state that the Scheduled Bank shall ensure that the maximum repayment period does not exceed 10 years from the date of first disbursement, inclusive of a 2-year moratorium on principal. The Financing Bank may curtail the period at its discretion.

application.submission_route: Submit the proposal with the complete Detailed Project Report through the Udyami Mitra Portal developed by the Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI).
application.bank_process: The Scheduled Bank appraises and sanctions the project, subject to approval of interest subvention under AHIDF, and forwards the application or project to the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying through an online mechanism.
application.interest_subvention_form: Application for interest subvention is to be submitted using the form attached at Annexure II.

fine_print: Loan under AHIDF cannot be used for acquisition of land by purchase, transfer, lease, accession or addition.
If the Eligible Entity does not already have the required land, it must acquire it at its own cost and complete associated land-acquisition processes before submitting the finance proposal.

Projects with land on a long-term lease of at least 30 years may be considered. The lease must have sufficient duration to secure the loan, and a No Objection Certificate from the competent authority for mortgage to the Bank may be required.

Documentary evidence of availability of land and applicable statutory clearances must be included in the Detailed Project Report or self-contained proposal. The Eligible Entity must provide evidence or a certificate that the land is free from encroachment and encumbrances.
Applicants must obtain all necessary clearances, permits and licences, and bear any related expenditure.
The State Animal Husbandry Department is to establish a single window to facilitate statutory clearances and handhold Eligible Entities.
Cost escalation caused by genuine reasons may be considered for enhancement of the loan amount within a reasonable time, but not more than two years from approval of the particular project.

For MSME-defined-ceiling projects, the Scheduled Bank's lending rate should not exceed 200 basis points plus the External Bench Mark Based Lending Rate (EBLR). Other projects may be charged a commercial interest rate determined by the Bank.

The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying pays interest subvention directly to the Scheduled Bank. First-year subvention is initially paid in advance based on the Bank's request; from the second year onward, it is released based on the entitlement claimed annually in advance for non-NPA borrowers.

A project is considered non-starter if no drawals are made within six months from the Scheduled Bank's sanction date. The sanction lapses if the Eligible Entity fails to ground the project within 12 months from sanction, although the lending Bank may decide on a case-by-case basis.
The Scheduled Bank may stop further disbursements until amounts in default are paid in full.

The Project Approval Committee approves projects costing up to Rs. 50 cr. for interest subvention. Projects above Rs. 50 cr. are recommended to the Project Sanctioning Committee after screening and evaluation.
The source states that the entire AHIDF amount of Rs. 15000 cr. is to be disbursed by Scheduled Banks within a period of 3 years starting from 2020-21.
Operational and credit-related decisions, including repayment process, penal interest, security and extent of finance, are decided by the Scheduled Bank subject to AHIDF provisions.
requirements: Prepare a Detailed Viable Project Report and self-contained proposal seeking an AHIDF loan.
Include a proposal for a quality management unit for milk, meat and animal feed, a packaging unit and product promotion.
Include future market generation, employment opportunity, raw-material procurement and other project-related information.

For dairy processing, meat processing, value addition and animal feed plant infrastructure, address suitable-site identification, engineering and socio-economic investigations and surveys, facility planning and design, and model studies wherever required.
Provide documentary evidence of land availability and applicable statutory clearances.

Obtain required permits, licences and clearances, including those applicable from local authorities, land authorities, State Pollution Control Boards, food-safety authorities and other relevant authorities.
Where applicable, provide MSME registration, company registration and labour or Employees' Provident Fund registration.

Application-form attachments include a detailed project with component-wise cost break-up, total cost, recurring cost, net income and project viability; proof of address; PAN/TIN/Aadhaar copy; MSME certificate if applicable; proof of land holding or ownership or lease and conversion; education and training certificates; income proof; and a bank statement for the last six months relevant to the project.
Provide the site plan, machinery and equipment list, and civil and machinery layout plan certified by a registered architect.

Provide statutory clearances required for the project, including local administration clearances, trade licences, Consent to Establish, Consent to Operate from the State Pollution Control Board and the required FSSAI licence.
Provide a roadmap for product quality management, product promotion and market development.
steps: Confirm that the applicant is one of the listed Eligible Entities and that the proposed activity falls within an eligible dairy processing, value-added dairy, meat processing, meat value-addition or animal-feed category.
Arrange the required land at the applicant's own cost and obtain documentary evidence of land availability and applicable statutory clearances before submitting the finance proposal.
Prepare the Detailed Viable Project Report and self-contained proposal with the required technical, financial, market, employment, quality-management, packaging and promotion information.
Submit the complete proposal through the SIDBI-developed Udyami Mitra Portal.
The Scheduled Bank conducts appraisal and sanctions the project, subject to AHIDF interest-subvention approval.
The Scheduled Bank forwards the sanctioned application or project to the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying online for interest-subvention approval, using the Annexure II form.
The Project Management Agency scrutinizes and appraises the Bank-sanctioned proposal for approval of interest subvention by the Project Approval Committee or Project Sanctioning Committee.
Projects up to Rs. 50 cr. are considered by the Project Approval Committee; projects above Rs. 50 cr. are recommended to the Project Sanctioning Committee after screening and evaluation.
After sanction and approval, comply with the Bank's disbursement, repayment, security, monitoring and project-grounding requirements.

records.name: India Post Franchise Outlet Scheme
records.objective: Provide increased access to postal services in urban and rural areas through counter-service franchise outlets where there is demand for postal services but a post office cannot be opened.
records.legal_basis: The Memorandum of Agreement references the relevant provisions of the Indian Post Office Act, 1898, and other relevant statutes, rules and regulations.

authority.department: Department of Posts, Government of India
authority.ministry: Ministry of Communications and Information Technology
authority.competent_authority: The Sr./Superintendent of Post Offices of the concerned Postal Divisional Office is stated to be the competent authority for grant of the licence under the Scheme.
authority.selection_and_agreement: The selected franchise signs a Memorandum of Agreement with the Department of Posts.

eligibility.applicants: Individuals, institutions, organizations and other entities such as corner shops, paanwalas, kiranawalas, stationery shops and small shopkeepers in urban and rural areas, including new upcoming urban townships, special economic zones, major highway projects, upcoming new industrial centres, colleges, polytechnics, universities and professional colleges.
eligibility.age: Above 18 years; no upper age limit.
eligibility.education: 8th class pass from a recognized school.
exclusions: Members of the family of serving postal employees are not eligible in the same Division in which the postal employee is working.

For this exclusion, family includes the spouse, except a separated spouse or one living separately while judicial separation proceedings are on; children and stepchildren, except where custody has been legally taken away from the serving postal employee; and other persons such as wards who are dependent on and normally live with the serving postal employee.
preferences: Applicants able to provide computer facilities.

records.benefit_summary: Right to operate a permitted India Post franchise outlet providing specified counter services and to earn commission or remuneration for services provided, according to the Schedule to the Memorandum of Agreement. Delivery and transmission continue through the Department of Posts.

details: Sale of stamps and stationery, including philatelic items.
Booking registered articles, including registered parcels; speed post articles, including speed post parcels; money orders on the EDBO model; e-post; and other stated counter services.
Bulk booking of registered and speed post articles, including registered parcels and speed post parcels, is allowed without any limit, subject to stated restrictions.
Functioning as a direct agent for PLI and providing related aftersales service, including collection of premia, subject to fulfilment of criteria for PLI agents.
Marketing products for which the Department has a corporate agency or tie-up and providing related follow-up services, subject to agreement with the other organizations involved.
Providing retail services, including sale of revenue stamps and CRF stamps.
Facilitating e-governance and citizen-centric services, subject to agreement with the other organizations involved.
Any other service introduced by the Department in future through its outlets that is considered amenable to the franchise model, subject to agreement with the other organizations involved.

details.service: Booking of Money Orders with value of Rs.100/- to Rs.200/-
Booking of Money Orders with value above Rs.200/-
Booking of Registered Articles and Speed Post Articles beyond 1000 articles, total of all two categories per month
details.commission: 20% additional commission for respective articles, i.e. Registered or Speed Post.

details.service: Sale of postage stamps and postal stationery, including philatelic items
Retail services, including sale of revenue stamps, central recruitment fee stamps, etc.
details.commission: 40% of commission earned by DoP, rounded off in rupees to be 40% or less

details.service: Monthly business from Speed Post Parcel, separately
Monthly business from Registered Parcel, separately

benefits.details: The Memorandum of Agreement states that commission on revenues generated and a fee for related services are paid by the Department of Posts monthly.

application.form: Application in prescribed proforma, Annex-I, followed by the Memorandum of Agreement in Annex-II for the selected franchise.
application.submission: The duly filled Application Form and other documents are to be submitted to the Sr./Superintendent of Post Offices of the concerned Postal Divisional Office.
application_contents: Applicant identity, nationality and age proof.
Department of Posts pensioner status, if applicable, with copy of PPO.
Income Tax PAN/GIR number, or Form 60 declaration if PAN/GIR is not provided.
Present and permanent addresses.
Location, ownership or rental/lease details of premises, validity of rental/lease agreement if applicable, and distance from the nearest Post Office.
Proposed business timings.
Previous retailing experience, computer knowledge and whether a computer will be used.
Reference from a respectable person of the locality.
Business plan, if enclosed.
Details of security required.
stated_processing_points: The office-use form states that authorization of the franchise is to be completed within 7 days from the date of receipt of the NSC.
The source also contains the text: “report from the ASP /SDI within 14 days from date of receipt of application.” The surrounding source text is incomplete.

fine_print: Only counter services are franchised; delivery and transmission continue through the Department of Posts.
The franchise must provide service across the counter for a minimum defined time schedule, with flexibility to work round the clock.
A franchise outlet will not book any money order for a value less than Rs.100/-.

Franchisees must not do bulk booking from BNPL customers. Restrictions imposed by the Department on outsourcing agents for bulk booking also apply to franchisees. No rebate for bulk booking of speed post articles is admissible over and above the commission payable to franchisees as applicable from time to time.
Continuation is subject to a first review 6 months after opening and a final decision 6 months thereafter, i.e. one year after opening.
The range of counter services may vary by outlet according to location and capacity to generate revenues.

The expected minimum revenue depends on the range of services, location, potential revenue, investments proposed by the franchise, cost likely to be incurred by the Department in providing support facilities and other stated factors; no fixed income is stated.
The Department may modify commission rates and the terms and conditions of the licence, including the amount of security deposit.
The franchise is independent and must not represent itself as an agent or partner of the Department of Posts or as entitled to pledge the Department's credit.
The franchise is not transferable. The franchisee remains responsible for breaches by the franchisee or employees.
Services must be provided at Department-specified tariffs or rates; breach may result in termination.

The franchise must remit actual revenue collected daily to the prescribed office without deducting commission, subject to the stated treatment of commission on postage stamps and postal stationery purchased on cash-down basis.
A minimum monthly guaranteed revenue to the Department may be prescribed from time to time, irrespective of the franchise's revenue level.
The franchise must provide linking arrangements between the outlet and designated Department offices and finance daily transactions where required.
The franchise must maintain accounts and records, permit inspection without notice, safeguard mail, documents and cash, and bear losses to the Department caused by failure to do so.
The franchise must obtain prior written consent from the Department for equipment purchases and prior approval for modification of layout or shifting premises.
The franchise must maintain insurance against loss or damage arising from fire, explosion, impart, burglary and other stated risks.

The Department may unilaterally terminate the agreement for stated defaults, false or misleading information, non-payment or non-submission, suspected disclosure of confidential information, or conduct not protecting the exclusivity of the marks. Remedial periods stated are 48 hours for a remediable service-quality default and one week for other remediable defaults; persistent default means more than three occurrences in any period of 12 consecutive months.
A franchisee wishing to terminate must give at least three months' notice, without being relieved of outstanding or subsequently due payments.

The source contains an incomplete text fragment referring to franchises being “granted in such Gram Panchayats where Panchayat Sanchar Sewa Kendras (PSSKs) are functioning under the Panchayat Sanchar Sewa Yojana Scheme.” The source does not provide the complete context or condition.

requirements.premises: Properly located, accessible and appropriately maintained premises with suitable display of approved signages.
requirements.investment_and_plan: The applicant must be willing to make necessary investments and provide details of how the premises will be run, opening hours, proposed investments, market conditions, product-marketing proposals, awareness of the customer base and role in the local community.
requirements.reference: One reference from a respectable person of the locality where the franchise is proposed is required to establish character and antecedents.
requirements.business_plan: A business plan is to be prepared taking into account the anticipated minimum level of business or revenue worked out by the Divisional Head for the specific franchise.

security_deposit.basis: The maximum possible level of financial transactions likely to be undertaken by the franchise in a day; the deposit is to be increased on the basis of average daily revenue.
security_deposit.agreement_conditions: The NSC security is to be irrevocable, non-negotiable, without recourse to the drawee and encashable merely on the instruction of the Department of Posts. The Department may increase the deposit, and whole or part of it may be forfeited for infringement at the Department's discretion.

requirements.technology: The franchise is required to be able to transact postal business on computers; ability to provide computer facilities is a stated preference.
requirements.training: Induction and other training are provided by the Department. Travel and stay costs of the franchisee or nominee during training, where necessary, are to be borne by the franchisee.

steps: Obtain the application form from the concerned Postal Divisional Office or use the prescribed Annex-I form.

Submit the completed form and other documents to the Sr./Superintendent of Post Offices of the concerned Postal Divisional Office, including the stated applicant, premises, reference, business-plan and security information.
Undergo the Department's selection process and, if selected, sign the Memorandum of Agreement in Annex-II.
Provide the required NSC security deposit; the office-use form states that authorization is to be completed within 7 days from receipt of the NSC.
Arrange the premises, approved signage, linking arrangements, staffing or nominee, computer capability and required training.
Operate the counter services at prescribed tariffs and hours, maintain records and remit revenue as required.
Remain subject to monitoring and the six-month and one-year continuation reviews.

The source states that postal agents get 5% commission in connection with purchase and sale of stamps and stationery, including philatelic items.

The In-charge of the Link Post Office ensures availability of stamps and stationery when postal agents come to the post office for purchase. Approved signages are provided by the Postal Divisional Office or Link Sub-Post Office.

The application form's office-use section states that authorization of the Postal Agent is to be completed within 7 days from the date of receipt of the application.

fine_print: Only counter services for postal stamps and stationery, including philatelic items, are franchised through Postal Agents.
Postal Agents must provide service across the counter for a minimum defined time schedule, with flexibility to work round the clock.
Postal Agents are not required to sign a Memorandum of Agreement with the Department and are not required to provide any security deposit for taking the agency.
Stamps and stationery are purchased from the Link Post Office by cash only, subject to the conditions stated in the source, and on production of the Photo Identity Card.
The source text around the cash-only and commission provision is fragmented; it states that postal agents purchase from their Link Post Office by cash only and get 5% commission.
A simple record of sales of stamps and stationery to postal agents is maintained separately for each agent by the Link Post Office.

records.name: Franchise Outlet Scheme
records.objective: Provide increased access to postal services through counter-service franchise outlets in areas where there is demand for postal services but a post office cannot be opened.
records.legal_basis: The Memorandum of Agreement recital refers to the relevant provisions of the Indian Post Office Act, 1898.
records.authority: Department of Posts, Government of India; selection and licensing by the concerned Divisional Head, with applications submitted to the Sr./Superintendent of Post Offices of the concerned Postal Divisional Office.
eligibility: Individuals, institutions, organizations and other entities, including corner shops, paanwalas, kiranawalas, stationery shops and small shopkeepers, in urban and rural areas and specified locations such as new urban townships, special economic zones, major highway projects, upcoming industrial centres, colleges, polytechnics, universities and professional colleges.

Members of the family of serving postal employees are not eligible in the same Division in which the postal employee works. The stated family members include the spouse, children and stepchildren subject to the stated custody and separation exclusions, and dependent wards who normally live with the employee.
Age: Above 18 years; no upper age limit. The application form separately states that the applicant should be 18 years or above on the date of application.
Educational qualification: 8th class pass from a recognized school.
Preference is given to postal pensioners and applicants able to provide computer facilities.
records.benefit_summary: Right to operate a selected counter-service postal franchise outlet and earn commissions or remuneration for specified postal, retail and related services, subject to the scheme, agreement and Department of Posts requirements.
benefits: Counter services may include sale of stamps and stationery, including philatelic items; booking registered and Speed Post articles and parcels; money orders under the EDBO model; e-post; direct-agent and related after-sales services for PLI subject to PLI-agent criteria; marketing products covered by Department corporate agency or tie-up agreements; retail services including revenue stamps and CRF stamps; e-governance and citizen-centric services subject to agreements; and other future services considered suitable for the franchise model.
Delivery and transmission continue to be handled by the Department of Posts; linking arrangements for the franchised outlet are to be provided by the franchise.

Commission schedule stated in the source includes: Rs.3.00 per booking of registered articles; Rs.5.00 per booking of Speed Post articles; Rs.3.50 for money orders valued at Rs.100/- to Rs.200/-; Rs.5.00 for money orders above Rs.200/-; 20% additional commission for registered or Speed Post articles beyond 1000 articles total per month; 5% of sale amount for postage stamps and postal stationery, including philatelic items; and 40% of commission earned by DoP for retail services including revenue stamps and central recruitment fee stamps.

For monthly business from Speed Post Parcels and Registered Parcels, the schedule states: up to Rs 5,00,000/- — 10% and 7%, respectively; Rs 5,00,001/- to 25,00,000/- — 15% and 10%; Rs 25,00,001/- to 1,00,00,000/- — 20% and 13%; Rs 1,00,00,001/- to 5,00,00,000/- — 25% and 16%; above Rs 500,00,000/- — 30% and 20%.

application.submission: The completed application form and other documents are to be submitted to the Sr./Superintendent of Post Offices of the concerned Postal Divisional Office, identified as the competent authority for grant of the licence under the scheme.
application.processing: The application form states that the franchise is to be authorized within 7 days from the date of receipt of the NSC.

fine_print: A properly located, accessible and maintained premises with approved signage is required.

The applicant must be willing to make necessary investments and provide details of operation, opening hours, proposed investments, market conditions, marketing proposals, customer base, local-community role and one reference from a respectable person of the locality to establish character and antecedents.
A business plan is to be prepared using the anticipated minimum level of business or revenue worked out by the Divisional Head for the specific franchise.

Security must be provided in the form of an NSC. The minimum security deposit is Rs.5,000/-, based on the maximum possible level of daily financial transactions and subject to increase based on average daily revenue or later Department determination.
Continuation is reviewed 6 months after opening and the final decision on continuation is taken 6 months thereafter, one year after opening.
The initial agreement term is one year from acceptance by DOP; subsequent terms are 3 years, subject to satisfactory work and conduct and DOP's discretion to renew.
The franchise is not transferable, must operate on business days and within the minimum hours specified by DOP, must use Department tariffs, maintain records and permit inspections.

DOP may unilaterally terminate the agreement under the stated default, false-information, non-payment, confidentiality, marks and other grounds. Remediable service defaults generally have 48 hours after written notice, other remediable defaults generally have one week, and persistent defaults occurring more than thrice in any 12 consecutive months have no grace period.
The franchise bears stated taxes and insurance obligations and must provide linking arrangements, safeguard articles, documents and cash, and return Department materials and marks on termination.
requirements: Appropriately located and accessible premises, properly maintained, with approved signage.
Necessary investment for conducting the business and proposed operating hours.
Business plan and information on anticipated business or revenue, market conditions, marketing and customer base.
One respectable local reference for character and antecedents.
Computer capability is preferred; the franchise must be able to transact postal business on computers.
NSC security deposit of at least Rs.5,000/- and any increased amount prescribed by DOP.
Compliance with the Indian Post Office Act, 1898, applicable rules, DOP requirements, tariffs, operating manuals and agreement terms.
steps: Obtain and submit the prescribed Annex-I application and supporting documents to the concerned Postal Divisional Office.

If selected, sign the Memorandum of Agreement in Annex-II and furnish the required NSC security.
Receive authorization after the stated form-processing step and complete induction training and operating requirements.
Operate the counter-service outlet, maintain the required records and premises, and undergo Department monitoring and review.

records.name: Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP) Scheme
records.objective: To refund currently un-refunded duties, taxes and levies at the Central, State and local level borne on exported products, including prior-stage cumulative indirect taxes on goods and services used in production and indirect duties, taxes and levies related to distribution of exported products; the scheme is intended to boost Indian exports and competitiveness.
records.legal_basis: RoDTEP Scheme Guidelines and Rates notified by the Centre. The source links Notification No. 19 (English) as the RoDTEP Notification.
authority: Centre, which notified the RoDTEP Scheme Guidelines and Rates
Customs, through which the scheme is implemented
Central Board of Indirect Taxes & Customs (CBIC), which maintains the electronic ledger for e-scrips
records.eligibility: The source states that RoDTEP support is available to eligible exporters. It does not provide further eligibility criteria.
records.benefit_summary: Eligible exporters receive RoDTEP support at a notified rate as a percentage of Freight On Board (FOB) value, with rebate for certain products subject to a value cap per unit, issued as a transferable duty credit or electronic scrip.
benefits: Remission of currently un-refunded duties, taxes and levies borne on exported products, including specified prior-stage and distribution-related indirect duties, taxes and levies.
Support at a notified rate expressed as a percentage of FOB value.
For certain export products, rebate subject to a value cap per unit of the exported product.
Transferable duty credit or electronic scrip maintained in an electronic ledger by CBIC.
Rates cover 8,555 tariff lines.

application.mechanism: The source states that the scheme is implemented by Customs through a simplified IT System. The rebate is issued as a transferable duty credit or electronic scrip maintained in an electronic ledger by CBIC.

fine_print: Rebate is not available for duties and taxes that have already been exempted, remitted or credited.
Rebate on certain export products is subject to a value cap per unit of the exported product.
The source does not state the notified rate for any particular product or tariff line.
The source does not state an application deadline or detailed filing procedure.
Apparel and made-ups exports also receive similar support under the RoSCTL scheme of the Ministry of Textiles.
requirements: The exporter must be an eligible exporter; the source does not define this term further.
The exported product must fall within the covered notified tariff lines or otherwise be a product for which RoDTEP support is available.
Applicable value caps and the exclusion for duties and taxes already exempted, remitted or credited must be observed.

records.name: Assistance for Common Facilities for Medical Device Clusters
records.objective: To strengthen the Medical Device clusters’ capacity for their sustained growth by creating “Common Infrastructure Facilities”.
records.legal_basis: Operational Guidelines for the Scheme “Strengthening of Medical Device Industry”, a Central Sector Scheme under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, dated 08th November, 2024; Chapter II, Assistance for Common Facilities.

intended_beneficiaries: Medical Devices manufacturing units in a cluster that have come together to form a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) to execute the project of developing common facility; there shall be a minimum of 5 Medical Device manufacturing units as members of the SPV.

Medical Devices clusters promoted by State Governments through a Project Implementing Agency that is a legal entity under Indian law with the foresight of the State Governments. Such a cluster may be exempted from formation of an SPV and will be deemed to be an SPV for this Scheme, provided separate accounts are maintained for project funds and an Executive Committee is set up for project implementation.
spv_criteria: The SPV or Executive Committee must have representatives from cluster members, financial institutions, State and Central Government, and an R&D organization.
An individual manufacturing unit cannot hold more than 50% in the SPV.
Medical Devices enterprises must hold at least 51% equity of the SPV.
The combined net worth of SPV members must be equivalent to the total grant amount applied for, and each SPV member must have a net worth of at least 1.5 times its proposed equity contribution.

SPV members must be legally independent entities without any related-party relationship with each other as described under Accounting Standard (AS) 18 of the Companies (Accounting Standard) Rules, 2006.

records.benefit_summary: Grant-in-aid for setting up Common Facilitation Centres in Medical Devices clusters: Rs. 20 Crore or 70% of the total cost of purchase of equipment and machinery, for Central / State Government funded entities (50% in respect of private entities), whichever is less.

benefits.grant_in_aid: Rs. 20 Crore or 70% of the total cost of purchase of equipment and machinery, for Central / State Government funded entities (50% in respect of private entities), whichever is less.
benefits.eligible_use: Setting up Common Facilities in Medical Devices clusters.
expected_benefits: Improvement in quality standards of medical devices.
Improvement in regulatory compliance specified for medical device.
Increased availability of trained personnel for Medical Devices clusters.
Increased competitiveness of Medical Devices units in the cluster.
Reduction in the manufacturing cost of Medical Devices.

application.applicant_submission: Applicants must submit a complete project proposal in the prescribed format to the Project Management Agency (PMA).
application.invitation_process: The PMA will invite project proposals through newspaper / website and set a cut-off date for receiving applications.
application.application_window: The application window is opened based on a notice issued by the Department from time to time.

fine_print: Grant-in-Aid from the Department of Pharmaceuticals will not be utilized towards the land component of the project or construction of a rest house, administrative buildings or any other building that, in the opinion of the SSC, may be categorized as non-essential construction for the technical requirements of the project.
The minimum contribution is stated as: “Minimum of 30% or 50% of the approved project cost has to be contributed by the entity or SPV, as the case may be respectively” for the project.

There will be no duplication of funding for the same component/intervention. SPVs may dovetail funds from other sources, provided there is no duplication; resources raised through such dovetailing are in addition to the 50% contribution of the SPV.
Assistance for administrative and other management support of the SPV during project implementation must not exceed 5% of the Grant-in-aid.

The proportionate contribution by the SPV or beneficiaries’ share must be made upfront. Necessary infrastructure such as land, access road, water and power supply must be in place or substantial progress must have been made before Department assistance is released. Where bank finance is involved, written commitment of the bank to release proportionate funds is necessary.
Project cost escalation above the sanctioned amount will be borne by the SPV. The Central Government will not accept financial liability arising from operation of a Common Facility.
The Project Implementing Agency / SPV is responsible for obtaining all necessary statutory clearances in a timely manner.
Grants-in-Aid are not available to individual production units owned by a member of the SPV.

The Common Facility may be used by SPV members and other Medical Device units on a user-charges basis decided by the SPV. Average user charges must be lower than prevailing market prices, with reasonable preference for SPV members.
Projects must be completed in 2 years. The SSC may grant an extension of 1 year for delays due to reasons not within the control of the SPV.
In-principle approval is valid for 6 months from the date of approval and automatically lapses if final approval is not accorded within 6 months, unless specifically extended by the SSC.

Assets acquired from Government assistance may not be disposed of, encumbered, or used for purposes other than those for which funds were released. If the SPV is liquidated, the Government of India has the first right to recover grant funds; grant-funded assets and unutilized funds vest with the Central Government.

project_proposal: Technical recommendation from a competent technical body.
Business Plan including cluster-unit manufacturing processes, gap analysis, and proposed Common Facility operations covering technology, marketing, quality control, testing, purchase and outsourcing.
Final projections and financial viability report.

Action Plan for enhancing competitiveness of cluster units and placing the cluster on a self-sustaining trajectory of growth, with direct linkages between identified impediments/bottlenecks and recommended measures.
Implementation schedule containing activity-wise time schedule, payment milestones, expected commissioning date, delay and expected risk, and monitorable quantified targets for reporting outcomes.
technical_recommendation_examples: For an ETP, the State Pollution Control Board may be the competent body.

For Research Labs and Testing Centres, NIPERs, IITs, CDL, Sree Chitra Tirunal Institute for Medical Sciences and Technology, NIITs, IISc, or Certified Medical Device Testing Laboratories notified by CDSCO (MD-40) may be competent authorities.
final_approval_conditions: Execution of a shareholders’ agreement and other related agreements between the SPV and its members.
Preparation of the Project Proposal by the SPV and its appraisal by the PMA.
Procurement of requisite land by the SPV.
Establishment of a project-specific account with Scheduled Commercial Banks by the SPV; the Department of Pharmaceuticals would credit funds into this account.
Tying up sources of funds for the balance amount.

steps: PMA invites project proposals through newspaper / website and sets a cut-off date.
Applicant submits a complete project proposal in the prescribed format to the PMA.
PMA scrutinizes the proposal and submits its appraisal report with recommendations to the SSC within one month of the last day for receipt of applications for consideration of in-principle approval.
SSC grants in-principle approval to applicants submitting a complete project proposal with technical recommendation and having availability of land.
Applicant fulfills the conditions under the guidelines within 6 months of first-stage approval, with guidance from the PMA where applicable.
SSC grants final approval after the project-specific SPV, agreements, appraised proposal, requisite land, project-specific bank account, and balance funding sources are in place.
Project is implemented within 2 years from approval, subject to any SSC-approved 1-year extension for delays outside the SPV’s control.

Funds are released in four 25% instalments: first instalment upon raising and depositing at least 25% of the SPV contribution and signing the Indemnity Bond; second against bills, 75% utilization of the first instalment and proportionate SPV expenditure; third against bills, 100% utilization of the first instalment, 75% utilization of the second instalment and proportionate SPV expenditure; fourth after 100% utilization of the second and third instalments and mobilization and expenditure of the SPV’s 100% share in proportion to the first three grants.

SPV submits the prescribed Utilization Certificate generated through the PFMS portal, certified by a Chartered Accountant and countersigned by the Head of the SPV; expenditure details must be uploaded in the CNA module of PFMS before subsequent instalments are processed.

records.name: Marginal Investment Scheme for Reducing Import Dependence
records.objective: To promote domestic production of key components, raw materials and accessories used in manufacturing of medical devices, including in-vitro diagnostic devices, in order to reduce dependence of Indian medical device manufacturers on imported key components and raw materials and increase the depth of domestic value chains.
records.legal_basis: Operational Guidelines for the Scheme “Strengthening of Medical Device Industry”, a Central Sector Scheme under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, dated 08th November, 2024; Chapter III, Marginal Investment Scheme for Reducing Import Dependence.

authority.department: Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, Government of India

eligibility: Central/State Government Organizations, Companies/LLPs registered in India, and Special Purpose Vehicles registered under the Companies Act or Societies Registration Act to manufacture key components, raw materials or accessories used in manufacturing finished medical devices, including in-vitro diagnostic medical devices.

Medical device or in-vitro diagnostic manufacturers having a manufacturing facility and/or intending to produce key components, input materials or accessories that may reduce import dependence and enhance the depth of domestic value chains.

Manufacturers of critical raw materials such as polymer, glass, metal, textile and paper, having a manufacturing facility and/or intending to manufacture medical-grade raw materials, components or accessories for use in medical-device or in-vitro-diagnostic applications.
Manufacturers or importers intending to manufacture any medical device or in-vitro diagnostic equipment that is on the GTE list and whose manufacture would lead to reduced import dependence.
records.benefit_summary: One-time capital subsidy on reimbursement basis for eligible investment in manufacturing key components, raw materials, finished devices or accessories to reduce import dependence.
benefits: For companies with turnover up to 250 crore: 20% of investment in the project or 10 crore, whichever is less.
For companies with turnover from 250 crore to 1,000 crore: 15% of investment in the project or 10 crore, whichever is less.
For companies with turnover above 1,000 crore: 10% of investment in the project or 10 crore, whichever is less.
Central/State Government Organizations: grant of 20% of investment in the eligible project or 10 crore, whichever is less.
The component has a total financial outlay of Rs. 180 crore and a physical target of 30 facilities: 15 facilities and Rs. 90 crore in Year 2, and 15 facilities and Rs. 90 crore in Year 3.

application.process: The PMA will invite project proposals through newspaper/website and set a cut-off date for receiving applications. The PMA will handhold applicants to get applications registered for manufacturing eligible key components, raw materials or accessories used in manufacturing finished medical devices to reduce import dependence.
application.application_definition: An application is submitted to the PMA in the prescribed application form with requisite information, supporting documents and application fee.
application.submission_deadline: A cut-off date will be specified in the PMA invitation; the source does not state a specific date.

fine_print: The incentive is a one-time capital subsidy on reimbursement basis.
The total project cost may include land, building, internal infrastructure, machinery and equipment, miscellaneous fixed assets and related utilities such as water supply, electricity and steam.
Subsidy or grant from the Department of Pharmaceuticals will be computed strictly on the basis of fixed investment excluding land costs.
Escalation in project cost above the sanctioned amount, due to any reason, will be borne by the Central/State Government, Private Institution or Manufacturer, as applicable.
The Department shall not accept any financial liability arising from operation of the project.
The applicant is responsible for obtaining all necessary statutory clearances in a timely manner.

The indicative list of eligible key components, raw materials and accessories is in Annexure-II. The SSC may include additional items, revise the list from time to time, or approve additional items beyond the list if recommended by the Technical Committee after scrutiny of applications.

In-principle approval is valid for 6 months from the date of approval. If final approval is not accorded within 6 months, the in-principle approval automatically lapses unless specifically extended by the SSC.

Details of the expected increase in Domestic Value Addition in the finished medical device.
Operation and Maintenance plan of the project.
Action Plan for making the project self-sustaining.
Identified impediments/bottlenecks and recommended measures for improvement.

Implementation schedule containing activity-wise time schedule, milestones for payments, expected date of commissioning, delay and expected risk, and monitorable quantified targets for reporting outcomes.
steps: PMA invites project proposals through newspaper/website and sets a cut-off date for receiving applications.

Applicants register their applications for manufacturing eligible key components, raw materials or accessories used in manufacturing finished medical devices to reduce import dependence, with assistance from the PMA.

records.name: Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0 – Selection of Category I and Category II AIFs
records.opportunity_type: Government fund-of-funds capital contribution opportunity for SEBI-registered Alternative Investment Funds
records.objective: To support startups by contributing to the corpus of eligible Category I and Category II AIFs registered with SEBI, which invest in equity, equity-linked instruments and debt instruments of startups. The Fund of Funds will not invest directly in startups.
records.legal_basis: Operational Guidelines for Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0, document reference P-38015/17/2025-STARTUP INDIA (E-212782).
records.authority: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT); Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) as the Implementation Agency initially; a further domestic Implementation Agency may be selected by DPIIT. A Venture Capital Investment Committee (VCIC) screens and recommends AIF proposals, and a sub-committee of the Board of the Implementation Agency sanctions proposals.

eligibility.fund_type: Category I or Category II AIF registered with SEBI.
eligibility.management: VCIC will consider AIFs managed by experienced professionals with proven track records for funding under the Scheme.

records.benefit_summary: Potential capital contribution to selected AIFs from the Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0, subject to segment-specific contribution limits, investment multipliers, selection, due diligence and sanction.

benefits.condition: The Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0 shall invest in or contribute to the corpus of selected eligible AIFs.
Commitments to AIFs are spread over the 16th and 17th Finance Commission Cycles.

details: Deep tech: 40% of the corpus of the AIF subject to max of Rs. 500 crore.
Smaller early-growth AIFs: 30% of the corpus of the AIF subject to max of Rs. 100 crore.
Tech-driven and innovative manufacturing: 30% of the corpus of the AIF subject to max of Rs. 200 crore.
Sector/stage agnostic: 25% of the corpus of the AIF subject to max of Rs. 180 crore.

benefits.condition: The Implementation Agency may take necessary measures, to the extent possible, to have representation in the Advisory Board or Limited Partner Advisory Committees of supported AIFs.

application.method: The Implementation Agency shall seek proposals from AIFs and conduct due diligence.
application.presentation: The AIF would make a detailed presentation to the VCIC.
post_selection_documents: Letter of Intent issued upon sanction.
Contribution Agreement signed with the individual AIF upon sanction.

fine_print: The total aggregate contribution in a selected AIF from various Fund of Funds of different Ministries of the Government of India and State Governments, whether operated directly or through implementing agencies, will be within 50% of the corpus of the AIF. The VCIC may adopt a lower limit based on market assessment.
The Implementation Agency is responsible for monitoring and ensuring compliance so that investments are channelized for the intended segments and comply with the AIF placement memorandum.
Selection should give due consideration to supporting startups beyond metro regions.

AIFs selected under the Scheme must use committed funds, along with the applicable segment-wise minimum investment multiplier, to fund startups recognized by DPIIT under the latest eligibility criteria notified in the Official Gazette.

If the full committed amount has not been released before an entity ceases to be recognized as a startup, balance funding may continue from the committed amount along with further nurturing of the entity.

The Implementation Agency must ensure mechanisms to prevent potential misuse, which may include requiring AIFs to conduct due diligence on beneficiary startups and disclose other Government support received.
Operating costs of the Implementation Agency are capped at 0.50% per annum of total commitments to AIFs and outstanding, net-off capital redemptions, and are met from the Scheme corpus.

Distributions from the Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0, both capital redeemed and returns earned, net-off utilisation of up to 5% of returns for capacity building of the startup ecosystem, will be deposited into the Consolidated Fund of India.

Up to 5% of returns may be earmarked for sensitization, workshops, capacity building, plug and play shared facilities, mentorship and regulatory support; utilisation and implementation are to be decided separately by DPIIT on the recommendation of the Empowered Committee.
No application deadline, application portal or specific proposal format is stated in the source.

requirements.requirement: The AIF must be a Category I or Category II AIF registered with SEBI.
The AIF should be managed by experienced professionals with proven track records for funding under the Scheme.

Deep tech segment: the Private Placement Memorandum must mention support for “Deep Tech Startups” as defined by DPIIT in point 1(n) of Gazette Notification G.S.R. 108(E) dated 4th February, 2026, and as amended from time to time by the Government.

Smaller early-growth stage segment: the Private Placement Memorandum must mention that at least 50% of the corpus will be dedicated to seed/early-stage stage funding and that funding of up to Rs. 10 crore per startup will be undertaken.

Tech-driven and innovative manufacturing segment: the Private Placement Memorandum must mention support for tech-driven innovative startups in at least one manufacturing-oriented champion sector as defined by the Government of India and as amended from time to time by the Government.
Sector/stage agnostic segment: the source states no additional Private Placement Memorandum requirements.
The AIF must meet the applicable segment-specific corpus, term or life, contribution cap and minimum investment multiplier parameters in Annexure-I.

steps: Prepare and submit a proposal to the Implementation Agency when proposals are sought.
Undergo due diligence by the Implementation Agency.
Make a detailed presentation to the Venture Capital Investment Committee.
Undergo VCIC screening and recommendation.
Undergo sanction consideration by a sub-committee of the Board of the Implementation Agency.
Upon sanction, receive a Letter of Intent.
Sign a Contribution Agreement with the individual AIF.
Invest committed funds in eligible DPIIT-recognized startups in accordance with the applicable segment-wise minimum investment multiplier and Scheme conditions.
Comply with monitoring, due diligence, disclosure and reporting requirements established by the Implementation Agency.
